intended_object: The automorphism group of a line bundle L on Y rigidified along s : T → Y with trivialization α : s^*L ≅ 𝒪_T. It is the subgroup of Aut(L) of automorphisms e with α ∘ s^*(e) = α. The source is the docstring and the module documentation (Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud §8.1, Kleiman §9.2).
explanation:
A `RigidifiedLineBundle s` consists of an invertible sheaf `L` on `Y` and an isomorphism `s^* L ≅ 𝟙_ T.Modules`. The definition takes the subgroup of `Aut L` whose elements `e` satisfy `(pullback s).map e.hom ≫ α.hom = α.hom`, which says that `s^*e` preserves the trivialization. This is the standard automorphism group of a rigidified line bundle. It also matches the notion of morphism the library uses for rigidified line bundles: in `mk_eq_mk_iff`, an isomorphism `e` must satisfy `s^*(e) ≫ β = α`, and for `P = Q` this is exactly the condition here.

The subgroup proofs are routine. The library goes on to prove that this subgroup is the kernel of `Γ(Y,𝒪_Y)ˣ → Γ(T,𝒪_T)ˣ`, which is the expected description of the automorphisms of a rigidified line bundle. So the definition behaves as intended.

The setting is the natural one: line bundles on schemes, rigidified along a morphism of schemes. Mathlib has no notion of rigidified line bundle or of its automorphism group. The construction could be phrased abstractly as the stabilizer of α under a functor in any category, but that would be a generic categorical device rather than a more standard form of this object. So the definition is not too narrow.
